trust_decision.summary: Grafana's Tempo and Loki backends decide that user-controlled path pieces (Loki resource URL, Tempo tag name, Tempo trace ID) must stay under the fixed upstream API prefix before being path-joined onto the datasource URL; at the pinned commit nothing enforces this, and path.Join resolves '..' segments.

landing_point.why: The Loki resource handler builds '/loki/api/v1/%s' straight from req.URL; it is the obvious 'path traversal in Loki data source' spot. For Tempo the equivalent is pkg/tsdb/tempo/tempo.go:291.

datasource plugin resource handler (core backend plugin)

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/ds/query with a Tempo queryType=traceId query (QueryData -> getTrace -> performTraceRequest -> createRequest, pkg/tsdb/tempo/tempo.go:111-112)
fix_sites.module_kind: datasource query path (lower-level request builder, separate file from the resource handler)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/tsdb/tempo/trace.go:189-198 (createRequest on the QueryData trace-by-ID path, not a resource endpoint; fix.diff:230-261)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report talks about resource/path endpoints; the trace-ID route is the query (QueryData) path that sends a fixed GET with Accept: protobuf, so a solver can argue the trace ID is 'just a query value' rather than a path. The Loki suggestions route (O8) already applies url.QueryEscape to the label name, so it looks escaped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Loki resource URLs carry LogQL in the query string (regexes like '.+', '..', '/'), and Tempo tag names are dotted ('span.http.url', 'resource.service.name'). A fix that rejects '.' or '..' anywhere in the raw string, instead of only whole path segments after decoding, breaks label/series lookups and dotted tag-values. The fix also deliberately allows paths that clean to exactly '/loki/api/v1'.

O6_input_shapes: raw '../' segments in the Loki resource path (fix.diff:198-206)
percent-encoded '%2e%2e%2f' in the Loki resource path, decoded by net/url.Parse before path.Clean (fix.diff:198-199)

Tempo tag that url.PathUnescape decodes after the query parameter was already decoded once (a double-encoding layer), checked per '/'-separated segment for '.' and '..' (pkg/tsdb/tempo/tempo.go:277-284; fix.diff:219-225)
Tempo trace ID with any non-hex character, rejected by an allow-list regex (fix.diff:246,255-257)

O7_producer.where: pkg/tsdb/loki/scopes.go:72-79 (GetSuggestions builds its own '/loki/api/v1/label/<name>/values' path from the JSON body and passes it to RawQuery)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Loki POST resources/suggestions: labelName from the JSON body goes through url.QueryEscape (which keeps '.' and turns '/' into %2F), then makeRawRequest's url.Parse decodes %2F and path.Join resolves the '..' segments; the published check only inspects the fixed outer '/loki/api/v1/suggestions' URL
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The label name is already escaped with url.QueryEscape, and the scopes/suggestions feature looks like a neighbouring feature reached only through POST, separate from the GET resource proxy in the report
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (scopes.go) from the landing point loki.go; same package; sink in api.go:257

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Tempo resource route (e.g. /tag-values-v1 or a per-scope tags route) that formats a user tag into an 'api/search/tag/%s/values' path through proxyToTempo
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Tempo has v1 and v2 tag APIs and the mux already pairs /tags with /tag-values; a maintainer adding v1 fallback would copy handleTagValues.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another body-supplied identifier (e.g. a detected_field name) formatted into a '/loki/api/v1/detected_field/<name>/values' path with url.QueryEscape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Loki has detected_field/<name>/values endpoints, and the suggestions code already builds paths from body fields this way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a trace-ID path built in a second place, e.g. a v1 fallback or a streaming/gRPC trace lookup that skips the hex check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getTrace already retries v1 after v2 (pkg/tsdb/tempo/trace.go:60-68), so a separate fallback builder is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal in an outbound URL path (upstream API prefix escape / SSRF-adjacent request-path confusion)
